note: The edit list for launch/video/out/demo-3min-silent.mp4, demo-3min-captions.srt and demo-60s-9x16.mp4. assemble.mjs reads it; cards.mjs renders the cards, pages and overlays it names. Sources are relative to launch/video/out/. kb is a slow push from one rect to another, [x, y, width] in source pixels (height is width * 9 / 16). cut is the transition into the next segment: 0 for a hard cut, otherwise a crossfade of that many seconds. url puts that address in a bar across the top. noteAt "low" puts a note above the caption instead of at the top. Captions are the voiceover, one cue per line of at most 42 characters; assemble.mjs refuses a longer cue or one faster than 17 characters a second, spreads each beat's cues over its span by length, and writes the voiceover with its timings to voiceover.txt.

beats.title: The Deck
captions: This is Kipdeck, built on agent-office.
Every coding agent is a unit at a console.
The office ranks who needs you first:
needs you, stuck, to review, working.
Every screen reads that one ranking.

beats.title: A funded issue
captions: Issue two on our public demo repo
holds 15 test tokens on Solana devnet,
in a vault only the program can move.
Anyone can fund it from the board
or a Blink, signing with their wallet.
Here a unit is hired for it.
It works in its own git worktree.

beats.title: The agent's pull request
captions: The new unit is already at work.
Here's one a unit finished earlier:
PR #4, for issue one.
It was opened on the repo itself.
A PR from a fork never counts.

beats.title: When a person merges
captions: When a person merges, the office
asks GitHub: merged by a user, not a bot,
with write access? PR #4 was merged
by its own operator: labelled self,
so it paid nothing. This is a replay.

beats.title: Admin approval
captions: Even then, nothing pays yet.
The payout waits in the review inbox
until an admin approves it
with a signature from their own wallet,
so no key on the server pays alone.

beats.title: The payout on Solana devnet
captions: On a counted merge, the bounty pays out.
Here's a real release from a test run,
with no GitHub merge behind it.
It needed two signatures:
the attester and the approver.
The program is native Rust, no Anchor.
Release fails unless both have signed.
Both keys are in the bounty's address,
so a bounty can't swap its signers.
After expiry, anyone can send a refund,
and it goes back to each funder.

beats.title: Proof of merge on Base Sepolia
captions: Every counted merge is also attested
on Base Sepolia with EAS.
Reputation lives on Base, where
the ERC-8004 registries are.

beats.title: The public board
captions: The board at slash pom is rebuilt
from chain data alone.
Every row links to its proof.
Shown here with test data.

beats.title: One task over x402
captions: Outsiders can pay for one task with x402.
The first request gets a 402.
This test payment settled on Base Sepolia.
The task is held until an admin approves.

beats.title: The GitHub Action
captions: Repos can skip the office entirely:
this Action runs the same merge checks.
So far only against a test GitHub API.
It's pinned to a commit: it holds a key.

beats.title: Security and source
captions: Testnet keys sit in owner-only files,
and workers never see them.
Nothing is audited yet: testnet only.
Everything on chain is new in this fork.
It's MIT, built on agent-office
by webdevcody. Thanks for watching.
